claims.statement: The Investment Policy Committee owns the global balanced mandate’s strategic weights and bands, while the cited rates-regime research explicitly does not set bands and the private-markets research does not determine client eligibility.

The strategic allocation is 45% global equities, 35% global fixed income, 10% real assets, and 10% private markets for eligible clients; for ineligible clients, the private-markets weight is reallocated pro rata across liquid sleeves.
Equities and fixed income have ±5-percentage-point tolerance bands, real assets has a ±3-point band, and private markets has no ordinary trading band because it is managed through commitment pacing.
A weight outside its stated tolerance band requires approval, and a mandate-specific tighter band governs over the cross-mandate discretion matrix.

In March 2026, the committee adopted reduced duration-diversification underwriting when setting the equity band, using the rates-regime research’s lower assessment of duration’s diversification benefit; this is why the equity band is now five rather than seven points.

The committee accepted the real-short-rate regime assumption as a working assumption, will review strategic weights against it at the 2026 annual review, and has not yet changed the strategic weights because of it.

For private markets, a denominator-effect drift above the strategic weight is neither a breach nor traded, whereas over-commitment is a pacing failure that must be escalated; unfunded commitments are subject to a binding limit of two years of liquid-portfolio spending.

The private-markets research supports a 10%–20% allocation only for eligible clients with a genuine ten-year horizon and favors secondaries and private credit while underweighting primary buyout within the allocation.

Private-markets eligibility is a documented regulatory determination rather than portfolio-manager discretion; qualified-client testing follows either threshold pathway in SEC Order IA-7104, and accredited-investor status is separately determined.

A pre-effective-date qualified-client determination may be carried forward only with its prior-threshold basis recorded and cannot support a new subscription on or after the order’s effective date; each determination must record its pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date.

Eligibility is necessary but insufficient for a private-markets commitment: suitability and the liquidity constraint must also be met, every commitment requires approval, and no authority tier may approve a commitment for an ineligible client.

The guide is reviewed annually and when cited research is re-issued or withdrawn; for a supporting note that is superseded or withdrawn, the bands guide provides for suspension and return to the prior committee-adopted level pending review, while the discretion matrix requires escalation and forbids managers from carrying forward a research-derived weight or directly adopting a replacement recommendation.

A research-note escalation records the superseded note, replacement if one exists, derived weights, and affected accounts; a cleared escalation must also record the condition, authority level, factual basis, and date.
The taxable-account fixed-income guide governs portfolio-manager holdings without escalation, while mandate-specific tighter bands prevail over the discretion matrix.

The taxable fixed-income sleeve comprises US Treasuries, agency MBS, investment-grade corporate credit, and municipal credit; non-US sovereign and emerging-market debt are assigned to the multi-asset sleeve.

The guide’s former top-bracket implementation specifies a 22% municipal target versus 18% neutral and a 28% investment-grade-corporate target versus 32% neutral; its paired-trade rule returns both to neutral when the municipal overweight is suspended.

The guide specifies an 18% municipal neutral weight without the private-activity concentration for clients below the top federal bracket; the former research grounds the concentration’s advantage in after-tax treatment for top-bracket holders.

Within the municipal allocation, no preferred sector may exceed 35%, and positions in standalone senior living, single-asset student housing, or single-obligor industrial-development paper require approval regardless of rating.
Municipal duration must remain in the eight-to-fifteen-year band; an extension beyond 15 years requires approval and cannot be approved portfolio-wide.

The former municipal overweight depended on an after-tax AMT case: specified post-1986 private-activity-bond interest is an AMT preference item, qualified 501(c)(3) bonds are excepted, and the 2025-06 note identified a phase-out-threshold reduction as a risk requiring immediate review and re-issue if tax treatment changes.

For taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, Revenue Procedure 2025-41 sets AMT exemptions of $90,100 for an unmarried individual and $140,200 for joint filers or surviving spouses, with phase-out beginning at $500,000 and $1,000,000 respectively, while preserving the specified-private-activity-bond treatment and stated exceptions.

Each target has a ±2-percentage-point market-value band measured at month end; ordinary drift beyond it is rebalanced at the next monthly cycle, and a weight outside its stated band requires approval.
Tax-loss harvesting in municipal credit must apply sector limits to the replacement bond, so a replacement that exceeds the preferred-sector cap is a settlement-date limit breach.

Because FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 is superseded, the guide suspends its derived municipal weight rather than carrying it forward; the paired corporate underweight is also suspended and both return to neutral, while the manager escalates rather than mechanically rebalancing, re-deriving, or directly adopting replacement research.
The guide is reviewed quarterly and out of cycle when a cited research note is re-issued or withdrawn; cleared escalations require a recorded condition, authority level, facts, and date.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 supersedes the 2025-06 edition for positions taken on or after 2026-05-01 while preserving the 2025-06 edition as the basis of record for positions taken while it stood; the re-issued research moves the desk view to neutral and withdraws the private-activity concentration.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41’s reduced AMT phase-out thresholds are the basis on which FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 concludes that the former municipal after-tax advantage no longer supports the overweight.

Neither a portfolio manager nor the research desk may turn FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04’s neutral view, sector preferences, or orderly-reduction observation into binding allocation or transition instructions; adoption of a replacement weight is a committee act.

The discretion matrix is the cross-mandate ceiling for discretionary mandates: mandate guides may impose tighter limits but cannot expand discretion, and the applicable mandate band determines the governing limit.

Authority is tiered by portfolio-manager, senior-manager, and committee limits: managers may hold a single issuer up to 3% of account market value, seniors up to 5% and may clear one escalation condition per account, while the committee is required above 5%, for more than one escalation condition, and for band exceptions.

Conditions requiring approval regardless of size include stated-band exceptions other than suspension-caused breaches, binding research-underweight sectors, concentrated-position hedges, municipal-duration extensions, and private-markets commitments after eligibility determination.

When a mandate-cited research note is superseded or withdrawn, its derived weight is suspended and must be escalated to the committee; the manager may not carry the old weight forward, re-derive a weight, or directly adopt the replacement recommendation, and the escalation identifies relevant notes, weights, and accounts.

Mandate guides define the immediate treatment of a research suspension: global multi-asset bands return to the prior committee-adopted level pending review, while taxable fixed income suspends the paired municipal overweight and corporate underweight to neutral and does not mechanically rebalance a suspension-caused breach.

Employer-security trading during a blackout, a private-markets commitment for an ineligible client, and a position breaching a stated regulatory requirement are non-clearable conditions rather than approvable exceptions.

Private-markets eligibility is a documented regulatory determination required before a strategy is offered, is separate from accredited-investor status, and remains insufficient without suitability and liquidity compliance; an eligibility determination without a recorded basis is treated as absent in audit.

Every cleared escalation must record the condition, clearing authority, specific facts, and date; without the recorded basis it is audited as an unapproved position and charged back to the clearing manager's file review.

A single-security position is concentrated when it exceeds 15% of the client’s liquid portfolio market value, with a lower threshold of more than 10% when the security is the client’s employer or an affiliate.

Concentration classification is separate from initiation authority: managers may take issuer positions up to 3% and senior managers up to 5% of account market value, while positions above 5% require committee approval and a written concentration rationale and remain subject to the concentrated-position suitability requirement.

Each concentrated position requires a documented suitability determination at acquisition and at every annual review that records the client’s reason for holding, unwind tax cost, and any restriction preventing an unwind.

A retention preference alone is not a suitability determination: the file must document that concentration risk was explained and the client’s decision was informed, and low tax basis does not excuse the determination or establish suitability.
Hedging a concentrated position requires D.3 approval regardless of size, and collars, prepaid forwards, and exchange funds require written treatment of tax consequences before execution.

For employer securities, the file must record applicable trading windows, blackout periods, pre-clearance requirements, and any Rule 10b5-1 plan; discretionary trading during a blackout is prohibited and cannot be cleared by approval.
Every concentrated position requires a written unwind plan reviewed annually; a plan unchanged in three consecutive reviews is evidence it is not being applied and must be escalated under D.4.
A cleared escalation must record the condition, clearing authority, facts relied on, and date; without that recorded basis it is treated in audit as an unapproved position.

Private-markets strategies may not be offered until eligibility is determined and documented; eligibility is a regulatory determination outside portfolio-manager discretion, and approval cannot clear an ineligible commitment.
Every private-markets commitment requires approval regardless of size, but that approval follows the eligibility determination and does not substitute for it.

Effective 2026-06-29, SEC Order IA-7104 provides qualified-client paths of at least $1,400,000 under management immediately after entering the advisory contract or a reasonable belief immediately before contract entry that net worth exceeds $2,700,000.
For the order's net-worth test, primary-residence value and debt secured by it up to fair market value are excluded, while a natural person's jointly held spousal assets may be included.

A pre-2026-06-29 qualified-client determination remains valid for its pre-effective-date contract or private-fund investment, but cannot support a contract or new subscription made on or after that date; the firm requires the carried-forward file to record its prior-threshold basis.

Accredited-investor status is assessed separately from qualified-client status because IA-7104 adjusts only rule 205-3 dollar tests and leaves Regulation D accredited-investor standards and the qualified-purchaser definition unchanged.

The firm requires each eligibility determination to record its pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date; the order additionally requires retained records of the dollar test and determination date, and an unrecorded basis is treated as no determination in audit.

Eligibility is necessary but insufficient: before commitment, the client must meet a separate suitability standard and a binding liquidity limit under which unfunded commitments may not exceed two years of liquid-portfolio spending.

Private-markets allocation is managed through commitment pacing rather than ordinary rebalancing: denominator-effect drift above strategic weight is not traded, while over-commitment drift is a pacing failure escalated under D.4.

Research editions and regulatory bulletins are frozen authorities, while internal guidance is living material revised in place; a position is reviewed against the research edition that applied when it was taken.

The US taxable fixed-income guide implements municipal research as binding targets and limits, including a 22% municipal target for top-bracket clients and research sector preferences that are binding limits.

A portfolio manager who finds research cited by a mandate guide superseded or withdrawn must suspend the derived weight and escalate to the committee; the manager may neither carry forward the prior weight nor directly adopt replacement research.
Regulatory requirements, including private-markets eligibility, are outside investment discretion and cannot be cleared through approval.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 identifies its AMT phase-out threshold premise as load-bearing and states that the municipal overweight does not survive a reduction that draws materially more top-bracket holders into AMT.

For taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 sets AMT exemption phase-out thresholds of $500,000 for unmarried filers and $1,000,000 for joint filers, keeps specified private-activity-bond interest as an AMT preference item, and preserves the qualified 501(c)(3) exception.
Private-markets research is limited to eligible clients with a genuine ten-year horizon and treats eligibility as a regulatory matter rather than a research conclusion.

SEC Order IA-7104 applies adjusted qualified-client tests from 2026-06-29, preserves a pre-effective-date determination only for its original contract or investment, and does not adjust accredited-investor or qualified-purchaser standards.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 changed the semiconductor-capex view from overweight to neutral for positions from 2026-03-01, and treats grid interconnection as limiting the rate of capacity addition rather than eventual demand.

A cleared escalation requires a record of the condition, clearing authority, specific facts relied on, and date; a private-markets eligibility record additionally requires pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date.
FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 supersedes FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 for positions taken on or after 2026-05-01, while 2025-06 remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 changes municipal research to neutral, withdraws the broad private-activity concentration, retains a modest qualified-501(c)(3) preference, and recommends no new non-501(c)(3) private-activity positions without recommending forced sales of existing positions.

Under the US taxable fixed-income guide, suspension of the municipal overweight also suspends the paired investment-grade-corporate underweight and returns both to their stated neutral references; a suspension-caused condition is not mechanically rebalanced as ordinary drift.

For plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01, DOL Release 2026-31’s wider discount-rate corridor, conditional contribution relief, and limited surplus uses supersede the pension-demand premise that supports FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03’s long-credit overweight, triggering that note’s announced-rule review condition.

The pension-demand research record and DOL funding-relief overlay do not themselves establish a binding portfolio weight: frozen research remains the historical basis of record for the position date, while binding weights belong to living internal guidance.

For taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, Revenue Procedure 2025-41 sets the AMT exemption amounts and reduces the exemption by $0.25 for every dollar of AMTI above $500,000 for an unmarried taxpayer and $1,000,000 for joint filers; those thresholds are not section 1(f)-indexed before 2030.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 supersedes FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 in its entirety for positions taken on or after 2026-05-01, while the former edition remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood; the replacement was re-issued out of cycle in response to Revenue Procedure 2025-41.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.4 preserves FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.2's specified-private-activity-bond preference treatment: the interest remains an item of tax preference and is included in AMTI, so the 2026 change alters threshold exposure rather than eliminating the preference.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.5 preserves qualified section 145 501(c)(3) bond interest as neither an AMT preference item nor AMTI; FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 consequently retains a modest preference for nonprofit hospitals and private higher education while withdrawing the airport special-facility preference because it is predominantly non-501(c)(3) private-activity issuance.
IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.1 supersedes Rev. Proc. 2024-58 section 2.11 in its entirety, separately from the change's effect on the municipal research premise.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 moves municipal credit from overweight to neutral and withdraws the private-activity concentration because its modelling places a majority of the formerly assumed-outside-AMT top-bracket client base inside AMT, reducing the after-tax advantage to approximately 15 basis points and inside transaction costs.

Because the taxable fixed-income guide cites superseded FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06, its derived municipal weight is suspended rather than carried forward; the paired municipal overweight and corporate underweight return to their neutral references, and the discretion matrix requires committee escalation rather than manager re-derivation or direct adoption of the replacement research view.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 recommends no new non-501(c)(3) private-activity positions, no forced sale of existing positions, and an orderly reduction; it retains the eight-to-fifteen-year duration preference, but these are research conclusions rather than binding allocation instructions.

DOL Release 2026-31 is a synthetic regulatory overlay for single-employer defined-benefit-plan funding rules, issued in 2026-08 and effective only for plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01; it is not portfolio guidance.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.2 widens the twenty-five-year-average segment-rate corridor from 10% to 20% for affected plan years, permitting higher discount rates and lower measured liabilities that will generally create surplus for plans near full funding under the former corridor.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.3 removes the minimum required contribution for a plan above 110% funded under P.2 and allows the sponsor to elect to treat the excess as available for P.4 purposes; P.4 limits those uses to a qualified replacement-plan transfer or retiree health accounts and does not authorize a sponsor reversion outside the existing statutory framework.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.5 preserves benefit-accrual, vesting, and all existing below-80%-funded-plan restrictions, and does not address fiduciary investment standards; P.6 requires participant notice within 30 days when a sponsor elects P.3 relief.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.2-P.4 prospectively invalidate the FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 L.2 pension-demand premise because that load-bearing premise depends on contribution requirements and the liability discount-rate basis making surplus worth protecting; the note expressly identifies surplus release, discount-rate changes, and reduced contribution requirements as risks that invalidate its overweight and requires review after an announced funding or discount-rate change.

FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03, published 2026-03-05 and applicable from 2026-04-01, remains the historical basis of record for positions taken while it stood; the prospective DOL overlay triggers review but does not retroactively rewrite that frozen research record.

The DOL release creates neither an investment-manager permission nor a long-credit allocation instruction: research provides a thesis, living guidance sets binding portfolio weights, and the available taxable fixed-income guide derives its stated weights from the municipal and IG-spreads notes rather than FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03.

The internal superseded-note escalation mechanism applies when a mandate guide cites the relevant research note: it suspends the derived weight, requires a record of the affected notes, weights, and accounts, and reserves adoption of a replacement binding weight to the committee; it does not create an LDI-specific response without that cited dependency.

SEC Order IA-7104, effective 2026-06-29, sets Rule 205-3's adjusted qualified-client tests at at least $1,400,000 under the adviser's management immediately after contract entry or an adviser's reasonable belief immediately before entry that net worth exceeds $2,700,000.

For the order's net-worth test, primary-residence value and debt secured by it up to fair market value are excluded, while a natural person may include jointly held spousal assets; the order does not modify those provisions.

A pre-2026-06-29 determination is preserved for the contract or private-fund investment entered before that date under Rule 205-3(c) transition treatment, but cannot support a contract or investment made on or after the effective date.

An adviser relying on an IA-7104 determination must retain Rule 204-2(a)(8) records of its basis, including the dollar test used and determination date; the internal eligibility guide operationalizes this with pathway, evidence, decision-maker, and date fields and treats a missing recorded basis as no determination in audit.

IA-7104 adjusts only Rule 205-3 dollar tests and expressly leaves Regulation D accredited-investor standards and the Investment Company Act section 2(a)(51) qualified-purchaser definition unchanged; the eligibility guide requires accredited-investor status to be determined separately.

The internal eligibility guide implements the order by deferring the qualified-client thresholds to IA-7104 and requiring carried-forward files to identify their prior-threshold basis, while prohibiting use of that basis for a new subscription on or after the effective date.

Private-markets eligibility must be determined and documented before an offer and is not within portfolio-manager discretion; although every private-markets commitment requires approval, no authority tier may clear a commitment for an ineligible client or a regulatory breach.

Eligibility does not replace the separate suitability and liquidity gate: the private-markets guide requires both before commitment, and the research framework limits unfunded private-markets commitments to two years of liquid-portfolio spending.
EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2025-06 remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood, including when they are reviewed after the note was superseded.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 supersedes EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2025-06 for positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, changing the recommendation from overweight to neutral while preserving the earlier edition as the historical record.

The 2025-06 historical overweight was a 12-to-18-month US semiconductor-capital-equipment view, expressed through capital equipment rather than fabless or memory, based on an early wafer-fab-equipment cycle after a Q4 2024 trough and two quarters of growth.

The 2025-06 view treated extended lithography and deposition lead times and reduced top-three-customer concentration as confirming quality evidence, attributing the latter to two new leading-edge logic-foundry customers.

The 2025-06 historical view identified capex-guidance cuts by either of the two largest logic customers, sustained memory pricing below cash cost, and material export-control shipment restrictions as signals that would change its view.

The current 2026-02 neutral recommendation is driven by valuation and a late-cycle position, not a deterioration in fundamentals: spending had risen for six quarters, lead times had ceased extending and shortened modestly in deposition, and the desk read that as an ordinary late-cycle rather than demand signal.

The 2026-02 downgrade does not rest on customer concentration: the top-three share improved to 46% and the desk preserved the earlier structural argument; at neutral it retains a lithography preference over deposition and etch on pricing-power grounds.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 is overweight regulated utilities with data-centre load growth and electrical-equipment makers with transformer and switchgear capacity, based on electrical infrastructure becoming the binding AI constraint through 2026; it holds no directional compute-vendor view.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 P.4 modifies EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.4: grid-interconnection timelines gate leading-edge fab siting and therefore cap the rate and timing of capacity additions, not the level of eventual semiconductor demand.

The global power view identifies an AI-capital-formation slowdown as a risk that would remove its load-growth premise, so the power overlay is not a standalone directional semiconductor end-demand conclusion.

Edition 2026-10 is a US Fixed Income Research market view published on 2026-10-06, applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-11-01; it changed the duration stance from neutral to a modest +0.4 years versus benchmark.
The duration-long recommendation is to be expressed in the 5–10-year sector, with a 2s10s-steepening bias rather than a parallel extension, and not through the long end.

The September 2026 FOMC raised the federal-funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, describing the stance as somewhat more restrictive and citing inflation elevated relative to its 2% objective.

The note's policy premise is one further increase over 12 months versus 1.5 increases market-implied, and it characterizes the half-step difference as the entire, modest basis for its duration recommendation.

The FOMC statement does not commit to a future adjustment sequence; it says additional adjustments will reflect cumulative effects, policy lags, and economic and financial developments, with assessment of incoming data and the evolving outlook at each meeting.

The desk avoids the long end because it sees term premium as fair to cheap, heavy long-end supply, and no catalyst for compression within 12 months, so long-end duration would express a term-premium view it does not hold.

The policy-path risk is inflation producing a sequence of increases rather than the assumed single increase; the statement reports three July dissents favoring hikes, while the September action was unanimous.
A fiscal increase in long-end supply and a disorderly term-premium repricing are distinct long-end risks; the note says the latter can still hurt the position despite its front-loaded expression.

The page is a research input rather than binding allocation guidance; the Investment Policy Committee owns the global allocation bands, and its discretion matrix says adopting a research view into a binding weight is a committee act rather than a portfolio-manager act.

FI-US-PENSION-LDI, Edition 2026-03 was published on 2026-03-05, applies to positions taken on or after 2026-04-01, and changed the desk view from neutral to overweight long-dated investment-grade credit.

The 2026-03 long-credit overweight is a demand and supply-flow view: it expects corporate defined-benefit plans to buy long corporate paper through 2028, with demand large relative to net long-end issuance; issuance had been below that demand for six quarters.
The FI-US-PENSION-LDI expression is bounded to the long end and single-A-and-better credit because it is a flow call rather than compensation for lower credit quality.

The load-bearing premise of FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 is that pension funding rules make surplus worth protecting through contribution requirements and liability discount-rate measurement; allowing surplus release or re-risking could reverse flows and invalidate the overweight.

The long-end pension-flow overweight and FI-US-IG-SPREADS 2025-09 have distinct scopes: the former is a maturity-specific flow view, while the latter is an index-level valuation underweight, not a credit-deterioration call.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.2-P.4 supersede the 2026-03 pension-demand premise prospectively for plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01 by widening the discount-rate corridor, conditionally relieving qualifying plans of minimum contributions, and allowing limited specified uses of excess assets.

DOL Release 2026-31 does not itself prescribe a long-credit trade: it does not address investment fiduciary standards, and FI-US-PENSION-LDI’s announced funding-rule trigger calls for review rather than an inferred replacement allocation.

Where a governing mandate depends on superseded or withdrawn research, the discretion matrix requires suspension of the affected research-derived weight and committee escalation rather than manager re-derivation or direct adoption of replacement research.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT Edition 2025-06 moved US municipal credit from neutral to overweight, expressed as a two-to-four-percentage-point taxable-fixed-income-sleeve increase concentrated in high-yield and lower-investment-grade private-activity bonds and funded from investment-grade corporate credit; it applies from 2025-07-01 and remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood.

FI-US-IG-SPREADS Edition 2025-09 is a separate valuation-driven, approximately four-percentage-point underweight in US investment-grade corporate credit whose proceeds are available for a higher-conviction taxable-sleeve position rather than cash.

The municipal overweight in FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT Edition 2025-06 rests on a load-bearing after-tax AMT phase-out-threshold premise for top-bracket holders; the note says that a reduction drawing materially more such holders into AMT makes its recommendation not survive, while fundamentals alone support only neutral to modest overweight.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT Edition 2026-04 applies from 2026-05-01, supersedes Edition 2025-06 for later positions, and sets municipal credit to neutral while retaining the eight-to-fifteen-year duration preference.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41 preserves the qualified-501(c)(3) AMT exception, and FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT Edition 2026-04 retains a modest preference for qualified-501(c)(3) nonprofit-hospital and private-higher-education obligations while withdrawing the predominantly non-501(c)(3) airport special-facility preference.

For taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, Revenue Procedure 2025-41 sets AMT exemptions and phase-out thresholds beginning at $500,000 for an unmarried filer and $1,000,000 for a joint return; FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT Edition 2026-04 models that change as invalidating the prior overweight's after-tax premise and withdraws the overweight.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.4 preserves the specified-private-activity-bond AMT preference treatment, so the regulatory event invalidates the municipal research's threshold-dependent after-tax rationale rather than eliminating the preference itself.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT Edition 2026-04 was re-issued out of cycle in response to Revenue Procedure 2025-41 under Edition 2025-06's review trigger; research replacement does not authorize a portfolio manager to select a binding replacement weight.

The taxable fixed-income allocation guide implements the historical paired trade through committee-set 22% municipal and 28% investment-grade-corporate targets; after supersession of a cited research note, it suspends the municipal overweight and paired corporate underweight, returns both to neutral, and requires escalation rather than automatic rebalancing or manager re-derivation.
The source note MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS 2025-12 is explicitly synthetic: its figures are invented and it is not research, a recommendation, or investment advice.

MA-GL-PRIVATE-MARKETS 2025-12 is a global initiation published on 2025-12-10 that applies to positions taken on or after 2026-01-01 and supports a 10–20% strategic private-markets allocation for eligible clients with a genuine ten-year horizon.
The research view applies only after eligibility is established; eligibility under qualified-client and accredited-investor thresholds is a regulatory matter rather than a research conclusion.

For global balanced mandates, the standing committee default is 10% private markets for eligible clients, while an ineligible client's private-markets sleeve is reallocated pro rata to liquid sleeves.
Within a private-markets allocation, the note favors secondaries and private credit and recommends an underweight, rather than avoidance, of primary buyout.
The desk identifies secondaries as the most attractive private-markets entry point because buyout-portfolio secondary discounts, though narrower, remain wide relative to the ten-year median.
The private-credit view treats spreads over broadly syndicated loans as adequate illiquidity compensation, while monitoring deteriorating covenant quality at the larger end of the market.

The horizon and liquidity conditions require a genuine ten-year horizon and underwriting to the client's spending requirement, with unfunded commitments capped at two years of liquid-portfolio spending.

No private-markets strategy may be offered before Compliance determines and documents eligibility; eligibility is necessary but insufficient because suitability and the V.6 liquidity constraint must also be met before commitment.

Private-markets exposure is controlled through commitment pacing rather than ordinary rebalancing: denominator-effect drift is not traded as a breach, whereas over-commitment drift is a pacing failure escalated under D.4.
Private markets has no ordinary tolerance band because it cannot be traded, and the note identifies prolonged exit-market closure and drawdown-driven denominator effects as key risks.

The allocation policy makes the V.6 unfunded-commitment liquidity constraint binding and suspends a research-supported band if its underlying note is superseded or withdrawn, pending committee review.
Eligibility documentation must capture the pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date; without a recorded basis, the determination is treated as absent in audit.

MA-GL-RATES-REGIME 2026-02 is a global Multi-Asset Research framework note published 5 February 2026, applicable from 1 March 2026; it has no directional recommendation and calls for strategic bands to be reviewed against R.2 and R.3.

The rates-regime note is a research input rather than the owner of binding allocation bands: R.4 says it does not set bands, while the global bands guide assigns the strategic default to committee guidance.
R.1 assumes real short rates have shifted from persistently negative post-2010 levels to a 0%–1.5% band through the cycle.

Under R.2, higher real short rates lower the equilibrium equity risk premium for duration-like equities and improve fixed income's attraction relative to post-2010 experience, which the desk says argues for a higher strategic fixed-income weight than the bands through 2023.
R.3 treats stock-bond correlation as unstable, including extended positive periods, and recommends underwriting duration's diversification benefit materially below the post-2010 sample implication.
In March 2026, the committee adopted reduced duration-diversification underwriting for setting the equity band, producing the current ±5-point equity band instead of the prior ±7-point band.
The committee has accepted R.1 as a working assumption and will review strategic weights at the 2026 annual review, but the current weights have not yet changed for it.

Existing global-balanced strategic weights are 45% equities, 35% fixed income, 10% real assets, and 10% private markets for eligible clients, with ordinary tolerance bands of ±5 points for equities and fixed income and ±3 points for real assets.

When a cited research note is superseded or withdrawn, the affected band is suspended and returns to the prior committee-adopted level pending review; the portfolio manager must escalate rather than carry forward the prior research-derived weight or adopt a replacement recommendation directly.

The research note identifies a demand shock returning the post-2010 regime and fiscal dominance holding nominal rates below inflation as direct invalidation risks to R.1, with the latter having opposite asset implications.

The corpus keeps research and regulator bulletins frozen while living guidance is revised in place; FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood even after supersession.

Binding mandate guidance and the discretion matrix constrain use of research: mandate-specific limits may be tighter than the matrix, but the matrix cannot broaden them, and regulatory requirements cannot be cleared through discretionary approval.

For the 2025-06 municipal basis, the taxable fixed-income guide set a 22% municipal target versus 18% neutral for top-bracket clients, paired with a 28% investment-grade-corporate target versus 32% neutral; the research described the municipal increase as two to four points funded from investment-grade corporate credit.

Municipal research 2025-06 identifies a reduction in the AMT phase-out threshold as invalidating its load-bearing after-tax premise and requires immediate review and re-issue for a covered tax-treatment change; Revenue Procedure 2025-41 applies from taxable years beginning 2026-01-01 and the 2026-04 edition was reissued out of cycle in response.

Revenue Procedure 2025-41 preserves specified private-activity-bond AMT preference treatment and the qualified-501(c)(3) exception; the 2026-04 replacement research withdraws the broad private-activity concentration but retains a modest preference for qualified-501(c)(3) hospital and private-higher-education obligations.

When a mandate-cited research note is superseded or withdrawn, the derived weight is suspended and the manager must escalate to the committee rather than carry forward or re-derive the prior weight or directly adopt replacement research.

For taxable fixed income, suspension of the municipal overweight also suspends the linked investment-grade-corporate underweight and returns both to neutral; a resulting band breach is not ordinary drift and is not automatically rebalanced.

A supersession escalation records the superseded and replacement notes, affected derived weights, and affected accounts; every cleared escalation also records the condition, authority level, facts relied upon, and date, with an undocumented clearance treated as unapproved in audit.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 applies from 2025-07-01, and FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2026-04 supersedes it for positions taken on or after 2026-05-01; the earlier edition remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood.
